newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 23.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 23.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer
Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Spending on traditional advertising in Germany grew by 3.5 percent to 13.4 billion marks ($7.3 billion) in the first half of this year, the Nielsen S+P resarch firm says. Private television stations provided the largest share of the boost, increasing revenues by 10.5 percent to 5.3 billion marks. Public TV, however, posted losses of 9.3 percent to 434.4 million marks. Print media had a "satisfactory" first half with a 0.6 percent climb in gross ad revenues to 6.4 percent (Horizont)
KRONBERG - The Kronberg-based media marketing firm IP
Deutschland plans to handle Germany-wide ad bookings for the Berlin radio station Energy 103.4. The station will be moving from marketing agency RMS to IP at the beginning of 1998, IP
says. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Industrial group Siemens AG says its semiconductor unit licensed technology from Sun Microsystems Inc for a new generation of smart cards. Siemens plans to use technology based on Java -- Sun's programming language that can run on different types of computers -- to make chips for credit-card sized cards that could store bank account, health and other personal
information. (Reuter)
BONN - Circulation of German newspapers and magazines dropped
slightly in the second quarter of 1997, the statistical
information centre of advertising media (IVW) says. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Live coverage of the Tour de France has won good
ratings winner for public network ARD, fueled by the success of
German Jan Ullrich. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
MUNICH - Television group ProSieben says it will distribute list
prices for TV advertising on August 1. The prices for ad spots
and ad blocks, based on prognoses of market share and
development, serve as an indicator of the expectations of the
station. ProSieben says private stations RTL and Sat1 usually
also release their prices on August 1. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
FRANKFURT - German economic growth will pick up pace as the year
goes on, but will undershoot the government's forecast of 2.5
percent expansion in 1997, a Reuters poll shows. (Reuter)
WOLFSBURG - Carmaker Volkswagen AG says that vehicle sales in
the first half of 1997 rose 9.8 percent to 2.194 million
vehicles. (Reuter)
BONN - Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says Europe must focus on
strengthening the Airbus consortium in response to a planned
merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas rather than block the $14
billion merger. (Reuter)
WIESBADEN - The statistics Office in the west German state of
North Hesse says the cost of living rose 0.5 percent in July
from June for an annual rate of 1.6 percent. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt blocks BASF AG's
attempt to sell its Kali & Salz unit to Canada's Potash Corp and
the company says the decision could put thousands of jobs in
jeopardy. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Car rental firm Sixt AG, reporting a 60 percent jump in
first half profits, says it expects full-year profits to rise
between 40 and 50 percent on a group turnover gain of some 25
percent. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Electronics and transport group Vossloh AG says that
it will be joining the MDAX index of medium-sized firms in the
autumn. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
LONDON - Germany's top television talk show host Thomas
Gottschalk has signed an exclusive global contract with U.S.
entertainment giant Walt Disney Co, sister firm Buena Vista
Productions International says. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - Michael Schroepfer is new marketing director of
Koening brewery in Duisberg. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - Tatjana Taphorn-Breloh is the fifth member of the
management team at Euro RSCG in Duesseldorf to step down in the
last few months. (Horizont)
